edges.subject: neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses
edges.quote: The high prevalence of gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms has prompted researchers and clinicians to move beyond an exclusively "brain-centric" perspective.

edges.subject: CLN genes
edges.quote: At the molecular level, mutations in CLN genes lead to lysosomal dysfunction and impaired autophagy, resulting in intracellular accumulation of storage material that disrupts both central and enteric neuronal homeostasis.

edges.subject: neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses
edges.quote: We found that the nature of GI symptoms was multifactorial in NCLs, involving not only the CNS but also the autonomic and enteric nervous systems, which were affected early by lysosomal deposits and enteric neuron degeneration.

edges.subject: gene therapy
edges.quote: Of note, preclinical studies showed that gene therapy could improve not only CNS manifestations but also GI ones, which may have beneficial implications for patient care.

edges.subject: neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses
edges.quote: GI involvement is a key feature of NCLs, with early impact on the enteric nervous system and possible links to gut microbiota.
